newsitem.title: CHINA: China fines polluting fertiliser factory.
newsitem.headline: China fines polluting fertiliser factory.

text.p: A court in southwest China has ordered a fertiliser plant to pay fishermen compensation of 1.68 million yuan ($202,000) for dumping waste into a lake, officials said on Monday.

The Guizhou provincial Higher People's Court ruled recently that the Guizhou fertiliser plant should pay 60 percent of the 2.81 million yuan ($339,000) in losses claimed by five fishbreeders on Hongfeng lake, a court official said by telephone.
Industrial wastewater from the plant had killed more than 210,000 kg (463,000 lb) of fish in late 1994, prompting the fishbreeders to sue the factory, the official said.
China's rivers and lakes are dotted with tens of thousands of factories, many of which have little or no waste water treatment facitilies.
The Economic Daily on Monday said the State Environmental Protection Agency had issued a circular calling for the closure of heavily polluting small-scale factories in 15 industries.
The agency said dirty paper factories, shoe factories and dye plants would have to close down or suspend operations by September 30, the newspaper said.
Plants producing mercury, arsenic, lead, asbestos, pesticides or other chemicals or metals would also face closures, the newspaper said. It gave no further details.
